messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Does anyone simulate Jackson Network in Simmer?
parts:
Jackson networks are just queueing networks with certain mathematical
properties. simmer is capable of simulating these networks and much
more complicated ones. The vignettes have examples of queueing systems
[1], where there's an example of an open network [2], and
Continuous-Time Markov Chains [3], which are more general processes.
This means that Jackson networks are particularly easy to simulate,
because everything is Poissonian and just "behaves".

[1] https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-06-queueing.html
[2] https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-06-queueing.html#queueing-networks
[3] https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-07-ctmc.html
